result:
Wrote `audit.md`. Verdict: **REVISE**.

The headline problem is one distortion that actually changes behavior: the draft scopes the draft→present→approve loop to project-level documents only — "Documents that describe the project (*rather than a single unit of work*) … explicitly approved before being written" — while the original requires approval three separate times for unit-level artifacts (`newtrack.md:46`, `:73`, `setup.md:142`). An implementation built to the draft could write a unit's spec and plan without ever showing them, and still satisfy every other line.

Beyond that:

- **Omitted** — two of the five context-document types are entirely absent (product guidelines: "Prose style / tone, Brand messaging, Visual identity principles"; and the code style guides directory). Also missing: the archive/delete/keep disposition offer on completion, user selection and confirmation of which unit to execute or undo, rewritten-history tolerance in undo, the coverage target and summary-location conventions, and the checkpoint record that makes resumption possible.
- **Distorted** — "Version control … is initialized if absent" is unconditional in the draft but greenfield-only in the original; the elicitation affordances from two different operations are merged into one stronger rule; and the §6 "ambiguity note" invents ambiguity about a point the original states plainly as a loop.
- **Mislabeled** — bounded one-at-a-time elicitation and checkpointed resume are hard specs demoted to ranked qualities #6 and #4; conversely the entire second paragraph of the activation boundary (the silence rules) has no textual basis in any of the five files.
- **Leaked means / fingerprints** overlap heavily — date-encoded identifiers, the per-unit folder triple, the markdown/JSON split, and "never on a single confirmation for permanent deletion" (which is `Confirm twice` barely disguised) are both over-constraining and identifying.

The audit notes that most of the leaked-means and fingerprint findings are the same sentences, so those two sections can be repaired together.
